key_insight: Pristine graphene flakes (GF) and graphene oxide flakes (GOF) behave very differently in perovskite systems: GF is a comparatively non-disruptive, chemically defined additive that helps preorganize precursors and improve crystallization, while GOF binds more strongly but perturbs the lattice and creates harmful local states.
engineering_relevance: Using GF as an additive can boost perovskite film formation, solar-cell efficiency, and storage stability, especially in compositions with difficult crystallization such as mixed Sn-Pb perovskites.
method: DFT calculations to compare flake chemistry, interfacial bonding, polarization, and electronic effects.
Machine-learning atomistic simulations of solvated perovskite nanocrystals with graphene flakes.
Solution spectroscopy to verify precursor preorganization and crystallization behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that GF improved mixed Sn-Pb device champion efficiency from 21.5% to 23.7% and also improved storage stability across perovskite compositions.
watch_item: GF performance depends on solvent and precursor environment, so implementation may require composition-specific and process-specific optimization rather than a one-size-fits-all additive recipe.
paper_title: Understanding Graphene-Perovskite Interactions: From Flake Chemistry to Crystallisation and Solar Cell Performance
